text: By the time Corwin reached the edge of the Ashfall Wastes, the sun had become a dull copper coin hanging behind a curtain of smoke, and his water skin held barely enough for a single day. He had left the monastery with three companions and a map drawn by a man who swore he had crossed the wastes twice; now the map was ash, the man was a liar, and the companions were graves he had dug with his own bleeding hands. Still, he walked. He walked because the letter in his coat was addressed to a queen who did not yet know her brother was alive, and because the boy who had handed it to him had died believing it would arrive. At night the wind spoke in voices he almost recognized, his father's laugh, his sister's lullaby, the old abbot reciting prayers in a language no one living could read, and Corwin learned to answer none of them. On the seventh day he found a well, dry and choked with bones, and he sat beside it for a long time, wondering whether stubbornness and courage were truly different things or merely the same stone seen from two sides. Then he stood, brushed the grey dust from his knees, and kept going, because the horizon had finally shown him something other than ruin: a thin silver line that might have been a river, or a road, or only another trick of the light.
notes: Texto autoral. Parágrafo único longo (entre 1200 e 1600 caracteres) com períodos extensos, enumerações e subordinadas. Avalia se o modelo mantém o parágrafo inteiro sem resumir, omitir trechos nem truncar.
